subject.title: [Feature]: WebUI notification system, cron job management popups, and context monitor integration

question: Should OpenClaw add a shared connected-Control-UI notification/action queue for cron results and context pressure, and what snooze/reschedule semantics should it use?
rationale: The missing behavior is real, but the durable boundary affects UI architecture, cron scheduling semantics, context UX, security/admin broadcast overlap, and related WebChat action work.

options.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
options.body: Add one Control UI notification/action contract and implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

options.title: Fold Into WebChat Actions
options.body: Treat this as part of the broader WebChat inline button/callback action contract so chat, cron, and notification actions share one callback path.

options.title: Defer In-App Popups
options.body: Keep existing inline context warnings, cron history, and Web Push settings until maintainers choose a larger notification roadmap.

recommendation.title: Design Shared UI Notifications First
recommendation.body: Add one Control UI notification/action contract and implement cron-result and context-pressure actions on top of it.

likelyOwner.reason: This crosses cron gateway behavior, notification delivery, and product UX boundaries where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
